# enums/flags

> Bit flags: flags Perm(read, write, exec) declares constants 1, 2, 4, ...

truck [enums](../enums.md) · [source](../../../registry/enums/flags.pkg)

```
flags Perm(read, write, exec)

let p = read | exec
print p                     // 5
print p & write != 0        // false
print Perm_name(p)          // read|exec
print Perm_parse("write|exec")  // 6
print Perm_all              // 7
```

Each name becomes a `const` with its own bit: the first is 1, the next
2, then 4, and so on, up to 63 names. Combine them with `|`, test them
with `&`. It also declares, named after the set:

| declaration | is |
|---|---|
| `const <Name>_count` | how many flags there are |
| `const <Name>_all` | every flag set |
| `fn <Name>_name(v: int) -> str` | the set flags' names joined by `\|`, in declaration order; other bits as a number at the end (`read\|64`); `""` for 0 |
| `fn <Name>_parse(s: str) -> int` | the flags named in `s`, separated by `\|` (spaces allowed); 0 for `""`, -1 if a name isn't a flag |

Use it at the top level, like `const`. The `bits` truck's `|=`, `&=` and
`~` go well with it: `p &= ~write`.

## Syntax

Kind: `statement`; flags `top`

```
flags {name: ident} ( {first: ident} [ , {n: ident} ]* )
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | name | — |
| `first` | name | — |
| `n` (optional) | name | — |

## Expands to

This package has no backend: each use is rewritten to the following
source, with `{slot}` replaced by what was written there, and compiled again.

```
const {first} = 1
{each c in ,}
const {c.n} = 1 << ({#c} + 1)
{end}
const {cat name "_count"} = {#,} + 1
const {cat name "_all"} = (1 << ({#,} + 1)) - 1
fn {cat name "_name"}({$v}: int) -> str
let {$b} = sb_new()
if {$v} & {first} != 0
sb_add({$b}, {quote first})
end
{each c in ,}
if {$v} & {c.n} != 0
if sb_len({$b}) > 0
sb_byte({$b}, '|')
end
sb_add({$b}, {quote c.n})
end
{end}
let {$rest} = {$v} & ({cat name "_all"} ^ -1)
if {$rest} != 0
if sb_len({$b}) > 0
sb_byte({$b}, '|')
end
sb_int({$b}, {$rest})
end
return sb_str({$b})
end
fn {cat name "_parse"}({$s}: str) -> int
let {$v} = 0
if str_trim({$s}) == ""
return 0
end
let {$parts} = str_split({$s}, '|')
let {$i} = 0
while {$i} < vec_len({$parts})
let {$p} = str_trim(vec_get_str({$parts}, {$i}))
let {$bit} = -1
if {$p} == {quote first}
{$bit} = {first}
end
{each c in ,}
if {$p} == {quote c.n}
{$bit} = {c.n}
end
{end}
if {$bit} < 0
return -1
end
{$v} = {$v} | {$bit}
{$i} = {$i} + 1
end
return {$v}
end
```
